heading: Floating drydock for United States Coast Guard Yard

tree.heading: In General.—
tree.text: Except as provided in subsection (b), the Commandant, using funds appropriated pursuant to section 1181, may not acquire, procure, or construct a floating dry dock for the Coast Guard Yard.

tree.heading: Permissible Acquisition, Procurement, or Construction Methods.—
tree.text: Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this section and section 1105(a), the Commandant may—

children.text: provide for an entity other than the Coast Guard to contract for the acquisition, procurement, or construction of a floating drydock by contract, purchase, or other agreement;
construct a floating drydock at the Coast Guard Yard; or
acquire or procure a commercially available floating drydock.

tree.heading: Design Standards and Construction Practices.—
tree.text: To the extent practicable, a floating drydock acquired, procured, or constructed under this section shall reflect commercial design standards and commercial construction practices that are consistent with the best interests of the Federal Government.

tree.heading: Berthing Requirement.—
tree.text: Any floating drydock acquired, procured, or constructed under subsection (b) shall be berthed at the Coast Guard Yard in Baltimore, Maryland, when lifting or maintaining vessels.

tree.heading: Floating Drydock Defined.—
tree.text: In this section, the term “floating drydock” means equipment that is—

children.text: constructed in the United States; and
capable of meeting the lifting and maintenance requirements of an Offshore Patrol Cutter or a National Security Cutter.

sourceCredit: (Added Pub. L. 119–60, div. G, title LXXII, § 7214(a), Dec. 18, 2025, 139 Stat. 1695.)
